top news.title: Pope Leo XIV presents Magnifica humanitas, his encyclical on AI, calling for AI regulation, protection for children against hypersexualized AI images, and more

tweets.author: @pontifex
tweets.text: Humanity, created by God in all its grandeur, is today facing a pivotal choice: either to construct a new Tower of Babel or to build the city in which God and humanity dwell together.  In Jesus Christ, this humanity in its grandeur becomes the Way, the Truth and the Life, opening the path for each of us to grow toward fullness.

tweets.author: @davidsacks
tweets.text: The Pope rightly warns that AI must serve human dignity, not become a tool of domination or exclusion.  But if we hand governments sweeping power over AI development in the name of safety, how do we prevent it from being used to censor, surveil, and control citizens — as Orwell foretold in 1984?  This is the real alignment problem

tweets.author: @deanwball
tweets.text: Reading the encyclical, I am reminded that the Vatican is fundamentally a city-state on the continent of Europe, and that its elites, which of course include the Pope himself, cannot resist the myopic preoccupations of the Eurocrat.  This document would be much improved if it were less enamored of the traditional academia/civil society talking points on AI

top news.title: Huawei says it aims to make 1.4nm chips by 2031 using its “LogicFolding” tech, which is based on its new Tau Scaling Law intended to bypass Moore's Law limits

tweets.author: @huawei
tweets.text: HUAWEI has presented the Tau (τ) Scaling Law, a new principle for guiding the future development of the semiconductor industry. By 2031, HUAWEI's high-end chips based on this law are expected to feature a transistor density that is equivalent to 14 Å (1.4 nm) processes.

tweets.author: @kyleichan
tweets.text: It obviously matters that Huawei announced this in English at a major international scientific conference. They're trying to send a message to the US that Huawei (and China) are basically able to make progress despite export controls. So take that for what it's worth.

tweets.author: @iancutress
tweets.text: Doesn't look like a huge breakthrough.  They're using a technique that's expected to be done by everyone - because they can't scale litho, they've accelerated other parts of the roadmap.  Logic splitting is best shown in AMD's 2021 roadmap.  It requires tight pitch TSVs and best in class HBI.  So even if it comes out in 2026/2027, Huawei still has a way to go to hit 14A equivalents by 2031 using SMIC multipatterning...  [image]

top news.title: X says it is cracking down on large accounts that have been gaming its revenue-sharing program by “programmatically reuploading content from smaller accounts”

tweets.author: @nikitabier
tweets.text: Over the past month, we have identified a number of large accounts that have been programmatically reuploading content from smaller accounts to game the revenue share program and circumvent crediting the original author.  We are now identifying these posts and allocating the impressions entirely to the creator.  If you have insightful commentary about a post, we recommend using the Share Video or Quote feature to ensure your posts are properly attributed.

tweets.author: @ianmiles
tweets.text: All true, and yet: 1) X still lacks proper native video editing tools.  The article system exists but isn't surfaced on the main timeline, which means long-form writing on X is effectively invisible to most of the audience that would read it.  Live streaming?  Forget about it.  2) X under-incentivizes original content because creators get no real metrics.  Other platforms give per-post earnings estimates.  On X we get a bimonthly payout with no breakdown of which content drove what, so creators are optimizing blind.  3) Whether a piece of content is a banger should be decided by the audience, not the algorithm or AI

tweets.author: @tomwarren
tweets.text: I wish all platforms did a lot more of this. There are far too many aggregator accounts on here that just post screenshots of people's work or regularly upload TikTok videos they didn't create without linking the original. The web was built on linking to sources
